context:
This is a research-then-write task: w1 collects the operative clauses
verbatim, w2 makes the call and records it in the same place/shape as the
existing scale-stress licensing decision doc, w3 reconciles the user-facing
files, w4 escalates if the call is negative. No platform code, no data
changes. If at any point the conclusion is uncertain, escalate to the user
rather than guessing — this is a liability question, not an engineering one.
description:
Follow-up to the merged canonical-JOB foundation (issue #289 Step 1). The
blind-spot audit flagged a redistribution-liability question that the earlier
synthetic generator specifically avoided:

The public `joinorder` benchmark now downloads a Parquet conversion of the
2013 IMDb snapshot from a BenchBox-hosted GitHub release asset
(`releases/download/data%2Fjoinorder-imdb-2013-v1/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1.tar.zst`,
pinned in `benchbox/core/joinorder/data_manifest.toml`). BenchBox is
documented and marketed for commercial cloud-warehouse benchmarking. The
"Information courtesy of IMDb (https://www.imdb.com). Used with permission."
attribution traces to permission granted to the JOB paper authors / for the
academic 2013 snapshot deposited on Harvard Dataverse (DOI 10.7910/DVN/2QYZBT)
under that deposit's terms. It is not currently established that BenchBox
re-hosting and redistributing that data, via a benchmarking tool used in
commercial contexts, is within IMDb's data terms or the Dataverse deposit's
license -- as opposed to BenchBox piggybacking on a permission that does not
extend to it.

This is a small, standalone TODO whose output is a decision record, not code
(except a possible `DATA-LICENSE.md` correction). It is RELEASE-RELEVANT: if
the review concludes re-hosting is not clearly permitted, the project must
either accept that risk explicitly or change the archive-fetch design (e.g.
fetch directly from Dataverse, drop the re-host, or restrict usage). Do not
leave that unresolved or silently shipped.

Independent of `joinorder-canonical-data-assurance` (data integrity),
`joinorder-accessibility-and-comparability`, and `joinorder-step1-housekeeping`.
`joinorder-scale-stress-decision-framework` establishes a
`_project/decisions/joinorder-scale-stress-licensing-<date>.md` convention for
the Step-2 (scale-stress) licensing question; this TODO is the Step-1 /
canonical-data counterpart -- put its ADR in the same `_project/decisions/`
directory with the same decision-doc shape.

anti_patterns.dont: change benchbox/core/joinorder/data_manifest.toml `url` or the data-fetch path in this TODO
anti_patterns.why: changing where the data comes from is the remediation TODO's job, gated on the ADR conclusion

anti_patterns.dont: conclude 'it's probably fine' without quoting the governing clauses
anti_patterns.instead: quote IMDb's terms and the Dataverse license verbatim in the ADR
anti_patterns.why: the whole point is a recorded, evidence-backed determination

anti_patterns.dont: silently ship a 'not clearly permitted' conclusion
anti_patterns.why: record either an explicit project-owner risk acceptance or a release-blocking remediation decision

preserves.behavior: DATA-LICENSE.md keeps the IMDb attribution string ('Information courtesy of IMDb ... Used with permission.') — refine the surrounding context, do not drop the attribution
If the conclusion is 'permitted', no functional change — the data-fetch path and manifest URL stay as-is

prior_art.concept: _project/decisions/ (directory exists; the joinorder-scale-stress-licensing-<date>.md naming/shape convention is documented in _project/TODO/main/planning/joinorder-scale-stress-decision-framework.yaml) — put the Step-1 licensing ADR here, same shape
benchbox/core/joinorder/DATA-LICENSE.md + docs/benchmarks/join-order.md 'License And Attribution' — existing data-licensing surfaces; reconcile (don't duplicate) with the ADR conclusion
benchbox/core/joinorder/data_manifest.toml `url` field (the GitHub release asset) — the artifact whose redistribution is in question; if remediation is 'fetch from Dataverse', this is what changes

verifications.description: The ADR exists in _project/decisions/ and states a determination with quoted governing terms
verifications.expected: an ADR file exists; it quotes IMDb's data terms and the Dataverse deposit license and states permitted / conditional / not-clear

verifications.description: DATA-LICENSE.md and join-order.md reflect the ADR conclusion
verifications.expected: both cite the specific governing terms / conditions identified by the ADR; docs-validate passes

verifications.command: uv run _project/scripts/todo_cli.py list --worktree=main | grep -i 'dataverse\|redistribut' || echo 'no remediation TODO (conclusion was positive)'
verifications.description: If conclusion is negative, a remediation or hardening TODO exists and the decision is explicit
verifications.expected: either a hardening TODO is listed with accepted-risk language, or the conclusion was positive and no remediation TODO is needed
